device.modelDescription: Step module of the ch-packs family: cleans one GitHub Actions job log into its steps, so later steps see the output a person would read and nothing else. A pure function of its input: no disk, no network, no state.

actionList.name: clean
actionList.description: Cleans one GitHub Actions job log, as the logs endpoint returns it, into steps. Strips the byte-order mark, the timestamp on every line, ANSI escapes (colours, hyperlinks, character sets) and every other character a screen does not show (controls, zero-width, bidi and filler characters), group markers, progress lines (a bare percentage, git's object and delta counters) and blank lines; keeps ##[error] and ##[warning] lines with their marker. A removed character leaves a space only where one keeps a token or a secret's value apart from the word before it, so a token coloured or split by a hidden character reaches ch-step-redact whole; a tab becomes a space. A step starts at its '##[group]Run <command>' header (the runner's, which echoes the command, lists a uses: step's inputs, or is empty; not a group a script opens) and is named after it; the header's own lines are dropped; post steps start at 'Post job cleanup.'; lines before the first step are the step '(top)'. Returns the steps in order, how many lines the log had and how many were kept. Every kept line is at most 20000 characters (ch-step-redact's input bound; redact masks a line before it cuts it to 500), and a longer one is never cut: it is replaced whole by "(a line of N characters, omitted)", with a private key's BEGIN or END marker beside it when the full line would have opened or closed a key block, and a line that is a bare key body by a stand-in key body, so ch-step-redact masks the lines after it as it would after the full line. A step's name is at most 200 characters: a longer one is cut at a space, with …, never inside a word.
